next.name: Hades
next.headline: Hades: ransomware that several vendors tie to the Evil Corp network
next.in_short: Hades is a ransomware family. Bleeping Computer reported in 2021 that Evil Corp switched to it to dodge sanctions. Other vendors track its operators under their own names, and one report covers Hades operators' tactics.

sentences.t: The catalogue lists Hades with one alias, Operation TrickyMouse.
Bleeping Computer reported in March 2021 that Evil Corp switched to Hades ransomware to evade sanctions.
Secureworks published a threat profile on GOLD WINTER, which the Malpedia page associates with Hades.
A later blog post lists Hades among the ransomware that Evil Corp developed. It describes Evil Corp as a sanctioned, Russia-based cybercrime network.
The same post says US sanctions have applied to Evil Corp since 2019. It notes that group names such as UNC2165 are each vendor's own tracking labels.
Accenture reported in March 2021 on an unknown threat group using Hades ransomware against victims.
According to PCrisk, Hades Locker is an updated version of WildFire Locker ransomware. It encrypts many types of data with AES.
The Malpedia page names Cobalt Strike, Meterpreter and Mimikatz among the tools in reports on Hades. It also lists Advanced IP Scanner in a report title.
The catalogue lists many tool names for Hades, including Olympic Destroyer, Running RAT, Gold Dragon and SOURGRAPE.
Secureworks published a report in June 2021 on the tactics and infrastructure of Hades ransomware operators.
Mandiant published a report in June 2022 on UNC2165 shifting to LockBit to evade sanctions. Its title, "To HADES and Back", points to an earlier Hades phase.
The Evil Corp post describes the group rebranding its ransomware and becoming an affiliate of RaaS operations such as LockBit and RansomHub.
Treat each link between Hades and a named group as that source's attribution, not settled fact. Check which vendor made it and when.
